verdict_before_fixes: Close to native but not clean. Locked terms (panduan program 2026, Jadualkan sesi perbincangan program, secara bertulis), greeting/sign-off convention, subject lengths, unsubscribe line and facts sourced from FACTS were already correct. Three defects found: an informal time format in the day7 body that DBP's own advisory service rejects for formal/email registers, an English-order 'ke atas'/'di antara' calque pair in the same email (both high-confidence items in ms-register-audit-rules.json), and an inconsistent no-name greeting fallback between the two files (lead-email.ts used 'Encik/Puan' while nurture-email.ts already used the correct 'Tuan/Puan').

fixes.before: ...tiga sesi hujung minggu berjadual, 9 pagi hingga 6 petang, mengikut tarikh...— kerja aplikasi dijalankan dalam perniagaan anda sendiri di antara sesi.
fixes.after: ...tiga sesi hujung minggu berjadual, 9.00 pagi hingga 6.00 petang, mengikut tarikh...— kerja aplikasi dijalankan dalam perniagaan anda sendiri antara sesi.
fixes.reason: ms-register-audit-rules.json high-confidence item (section 5 Do 7): DBP Khidmat Nasihat gives the written standard as 'pukul 9.00 pagi', not the newspaper shorthand '9 pagi'; e-mails are a formal context. 'di antara sesi' is a calque — 'di antara' is not a Kamus Dewan headword for the temporal sense; the correct form is bare 'antara sesi' (audit item 6.11, high confidence).

fixes.before: Bimbingan bersama kerja aplikasi ke atas perniagaan anda sendiri
fixes.after: Bimbingan bersama kerja aplikasi berdasarkan perniagaan anda sendiri
fixes.reason: ms-register-audit-rules.json item 6.11 (high confidence): 'ke atas perniagaan anda' calques English 'on your business'; DBP glosses 'ke atas' only directionally/for imposition ('dikenakan ke atas'), not as a general preposition. 'berdasarkan' keeps the meaning without the calque.

fixes.field: no-name fallback greeting term for ms
fixes.reason: R3.1-writer.json's own reviewer note records the intended convention as 'Salam sejahtera, {Nama},' with fallback 'Tuan/Puan' (also used consistently in nurture-email.ts, both the HTML/text greeting default and the text-mode fallback). lead-email.ts had drifted to 'Encik/Puan', an inconsistency across the two files handling the same audience.
